test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Where is Wadge Bank, the site of the hydrocarbon exploration project proposed in May 2025 under the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) and opposed by fishermen, located?

options.text: An offshore reef near the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal region
A deep-sea basin around 60 km west of Mumbai in the Arabian Sea
A coral atoll close to the Lakshadweep islands in the Indian Ocean
A submarine plateau about 80 km off the southern coast in the Indian Ocean

solution:
The correct answer is **__option 4__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **It is a submarine plateau (underwater raised region)** located in the Indian Ocean.
 
• **It lies about 80 km south of India’s mainland**, near Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin).
 
• **It is one of India's richest fishing grounds**, supporting many coastal fishermen, especially from Tamil Nadu.
 
• **It recently came into news because fishermen opposed a proposed hydrocarbon exploration project there** under the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), fearing ecological and livelihood damage.
 
• **Swajal Dhara Yojana:**
 
 
• **Swajal Dhara Yojana** was launched in **2002-03** by Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** to ensure clean drinking water availability in villages.
 
• The scheme requires **10% of the project cost** to be contributed by villagers, while the remaining **90%** is funded by the **Union Government**.
 
• It emphasizes community participation in water management and aims to address water scarcity efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Universal Health Insurance Plan:**
 
 
• The **Universal Health Insurance Scheme** (**UHIS**) was introduced in **2003-04** by the Government of India, targeting families below the poverty line.
 
• It offers subsidized health insurance coverage and aims to provide financial protection against medical expenses to economically disadvantaged groups.
 
• The scheme is designed to cover hospitalization costs and promote access to healthcare facilities for the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Hariyali Project:**
 
 
• The **Hariyali Project** was launched in **January 2003** to promote watershed development through **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.
 
• It integrates existing programs like the **Integrated Wastelands Development Programme (IWDP)**, **Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)**, and **Desert Development Programme (DDP)** for environmental sustainability.
 
• The initiative focuses on empowering local governance structures for effective implementation of watershed projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Nutrition Mission (NNM):**

 
 
• Also known as **Poshan Abhiyaan**, launched by the Government of India, aiming to reduce stunting, undernutrition, and anemia among children, women, and adolescents.
 
• Focuses on **behavioral changes**, inter-ministerial and inter-departmental convergence, and capacity building.
 
• Target: Reduce stunting by **2% per annum**, underweight prevalence by **2% per annum**, and anemia by **3% per annum**.
 
 
 
• **Swajal Dhara Yojana:**
 
 
• A community-based water supply scheme launched to address water scarcity in rural areas and ensure sustainable water management.
 
• Promotes equity by involving local communities in decision-making and emphasizes the need for proper maintenance of water resources.
 
 
 
• **Universal Health Insurance Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme covers hospitalization expenses up to **Rs. 30,000**, compensates for accidental death or partial disability, and provides daily hospital expenses.
 
• It is managed by **public sector insurance companies**, ensuring that health services are accessible to low-income families.
 
 
 
• **Hariyali Project:**
 
 
• Focuses on sustainable development, afforestation, and improving soil and water conservation measures to combat drought and desertification.
 
• Encourages participation of local governing bodies to ensure effective implementation of watershed programs.
